narrow: The original quantifier exchange is false. On \(u\leftrightarrow v\) and \(u\to v\), with target \(C=\{v\}\), let source \(T_s\) carry value \(s\in\{0,1\}\) for \(u\), and let branch \(\omega_x\) request value \(x\) for the parent subscript of \(v\). Then \(T_s\) fails exactly when \(s=x\): in that case \(\{u,v\}\) is a connected-ancestor obstruction, while for \(s\ne x\) the matching arc is absent and the source succeeds. Thus \(T_1\) serves \(\omega_0\) and \(T_0\) serves \(\omega_1\), but no source serves both. Positive full-READ slices expose both sources without violating physical source typing. The proposed claim is the strongest unconditional consequence of complete exhaustive acceptance: one finite witness per factor branch, with an explicit \(\sum_j|\Omega_j|\) bound.

closed_note: Close PR 00e62adb568f. The PR correctly refutes uniform source selection, supplies the valid branchwise replacement, and identifies the obsolete uniform-normalization and embedded-uniform-certificate objects. However, its downstream repair restricts the main optimization problem to instances already admitting a uniform certificate. That assumes away the exhibited obstruction, can assign +infinity to a physically acquired collection accepted by complete CTFIDU+, and collapses the advertised physical-acquisition and ordinary-equivalence result class. Re-solve with an explicit branch-indexed switching-certificate interface and retain uniform certificates only as a restricted corollary.
